answer: Each identity registers a garden evaporation bed and locks a 75-credit bond. The bed fills at dawn; its harvest is dried by its horizon date. Each evaporation log is sealed by cipher, so the auditor can check it against the bed record: a mismatch above 3 percent, a reused log, or one key claiming two beds burns the bond. First fee 40; the kth pays 40 plus 5 times k minus 1, so the thousandth fake bed costs 5035. One thousand fakes pay 2,537,500 plus 75,000 locked. A rented-bed ring fails: each log is cipher-sealed, duplicates rejected. An honest harvester pays 40 once and recovers its bond.
